parole.significato: pre-eternity, eternity without beginning; the era before God created space and time
parole.testo: Borrowed from Arabic أَزَل (ʔazal), from Middle Persian 𐭫𐭠𐭮 (ʾsl /⁠asar⁠/, “endless”), from 𐭠 (ʾ- /⁠a-⁠/, “un-, without”) + 𐭫𐭮 (sl /⁠sar⁠/, “head; beginning; end”, whence modern سر (sar)).
Reborrowed from Arabic أَوَان (ʔawān), from Middle Persian ʾwʾm, ʾʾwʾm (āwām, “time, space of time; age, epoch; point of time, occasion”).
Borrowed from Arabic جَاه (jāh), from Middle Persian [Book Pahlavi needed] (gʾs), 𐫃𐫀𐫍 (gʾh /⁠gāh⁠/, “place, throne, bed; time”). Doublet of گاه (gâh), see there for more.
Borrowed from Arabic جَوْز (jawz), from Middle Persian 𐭢𐭥𐭦 (gōz, “walnut”). Doublet of گوز (gōz). See Old Armenian ընկոյզ (ənkoyz) for etymology.
Borrowed from Arabic خَنْدَق (ḵandaq), from Middle Persian *handag (whence Persian هندک (handak, “moat”)).

The form from Arabic دِهْقَان (dihqān), from Middle Persian [script needed] (dhywkʾn' /⁠dahigān⁠/, “countryman, farmer”), also found as دهگان (dehgân) and دهخان (dehxân). By surface analysis, ده (deh, “village”) + ـگان (-gân, “pertaining to, -er”). Akin to Old Armenian դեհկան-ութիւն (dehkan-utʻiwn),
Borrowed from Arabic دِيبَاجَة (dībāja), from Middle Persian [script needed] (dypʾk' /⁠dēbāg⁠/, “brocade”).

Borrowed from Arabic زَنْبَق (zanbaq), from Middle Persian [script needed] (cmbk' /⁠čambak⁠/) (whence Old Armenian ճանբակ (čanbak)), related to Urdu چمپا / Hindi चंपा (campā), Punjabi چمپا (čampā, “jasmine in the broad sense”), which has been borrowed into Persian as چمپا (čampâ, “jasmine”). Reborrowed from Arabic زَنْد (zand), from Middle Persian [script needed] (zng /⁠zang⁠/, “ankle, shank”). Cognate with English shank.
Borrowed from Arabic زِنْدِيق (zindīq), from Middle Persian [script needed] (zndyk' /⁠zandīk⁠/, “heretic, Manichaean”).
Reborrowed from Arabic سُكَّان (sukkān, “rudder”), from Middle Persian *sukān. Compare Parthian swk (suk, “rudder”).
From Arabic verbal noun سُكْر (sukr). Perhaps extracted from the root of Arabic مُسْكِر (muskir), from Middle Persian mstgr (mastgar, “inebriating”).
Borrowed from Arabic صَنْدَل (ṣandal), from Middle Persian cndl (čandal), from Sanskrit चन्दन (candana). Doublet of چندل, which was inherited from Middle Persian.
Borrowed from Arabic [Term?], itself borrowed from Middle Persian [Book Pahlavi needed] (tʾk' /⁠tāg⁠/, “item; unit; single; branch”). Doublet of تا (tâ), which is inherited.
Borrowed from Arabic أَطْنَاب (ʔaṭnāb), plural of طُنُب (ṭunub, “rope”). Majorly displaced native رَسَن (rasan) and اَرویس (arvês) (from Middle Persian [script needed] (’lwys /⁠arwēs⁠/)).
Borrowed from Arabic فُنْدُق (funduq), borrowed from Middle Persian pndk' (pondik), borrowed from Ancient Greek Ποντικὸν κάρυον (Pontikòn káruon), from Ποντῐκόν (Pontĭkón) + κᾰ́ρῠον (kắrŭon).
Borrowed from Arabic فَوْج (fawj), from فَيْج (fayj), borrowed from Middle Persian pdk'. Doublet of پیک (peyk).
Borrowed from Arabic فِيل (fīl), borrowed from Middle Persian pyl (/⁠pīl⁠/), from Akkadian 𒄠𒋛 (pīru). Doublet of پیل (pil).

Reborrowed from Arabic قَبَاء (qabāʔ), from Middle Persian [script needed] (kpʾh /⁠kabāh⁠/, “garment, cloak”). Ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *(s)kep- (“to split, cut”). Cognate to Central Kurdish کەوا (kewa, “long garment open in front”) and Khotanese [script needed] (khapa, “dress”). Perhaps
Borrowed from Arabic قَيْرَوَان (qayrawān), from Middle Persian kʾlwʾn'.
Borrowed from Arabic مِسْوَاك (miswāk), derived from سِوَاك (siwāk), from Middle Persian *sawāg (whence also synonymous سواک (sevâk)).
